capture_failure_rules: Never overwrite an existing valid capture; a valid capture is immutable once sealed.
Preserve failed/partial attempts under a separate, provenance-labelled sibling path, never inside the canonical output directory.
A pre-launch failure does not count as a scientific capture and is excluded from sealing.

A capture is canonical only after: trace file existence is confirmed, normalize() succeeds, reconcile() returns [], AND the explicit trace_completeness() check (argine/research/runner.py) also passes -- a trace is never accepted solely because normalize()/reconcile() are clean (instruction #20).
A malformed or incomplete trace is rejected, its provenance is preserved for the record, and it is never reused or silently discarded.
A retry must use the identical frozen acquisition parameters -- no parameter may be changed in response to a prior failure or in response to any observed model output.
No prompt or configuration change is permitted in response to model output at any point in this protocol.
No parallel capture writers: captures are executed strictly sequentially, one workload at a time.
A timeout during capture is not a PASS and must not be recorded as a successful cell.
cli_split_flag_gap_and_resolution: Identical gap/resolution as R2-BRIDGE-01: argine.research.cli's 'research trace --split' only supports {dev, eval}. The 12 R2-11 workload files' CLI-facing 'split' field is set to 'eval' (already-supported value); true provenance identity is tracked via provenance_split_identity='r2_11_eval', workload_id/path, and this eval_manifest.json -- never a new CLI value.
explicitly_not_performed_in_this_phase: No preflight executed on a real host.
No R2_11_CAPTURED_SEALED transition (no real trace exists).
No R2-11 performance/result computed, inspected, or claimed.
